title: Readings outside what the radio chips can report land as missing in staging; both edges are kept
reasoning: lnk_06: "Impossible values (a corrupt RSSI, an SNR beyond what the chip can report, a value that is not a number) are treated as missing and fail the rule." Casey set the limits on PR #72: SNR "-32 to 31.75 dB" (Q2), and for RSSI "(b), -196 to +115 dBm, cited to SX1276/77/78/79 sections 3.5.5 and 6.4 (both ports and the slope correction)". Both ranges are inclusive.
s13-m001: SNR -32.0 dB and RSSI -196 dBm, both lower edges: kept as sent.
s13-m002: SNR -32.25 dB and RSSI -197 dBm, one step below each edge: both land as missing.
s13-m003: SNR 31.75 dB and RSSI 115 dBm, both upper edges: kept as sent.
s13-m004: SNR 32.0 dB and RSSI 116 dBm, one step above each edge: both land as missing.
s13-m005: SNR 5.0 dB with RSSI 116 dBm, and s13-m006: SNR 32.0 dB with RSSI -90 dBm: only the impossible reading lands as missing; the other is kept as sent.
s13-m007: RSSI -190 dBm and s13-m008: RSSI 99 dBm, one step past the earlier limits of -189 and +98 dBm (Casey's Q2, before his RSSI answer): inside the range now, so kept as sent, with SNR 5.0 dB.
Every row has relay_node null, so none is a receipt (lnk_01) and none enters lnk_06's count of excluded receipts. The staging values alone are compared, by assert_lnk_06_chip_range_edges.
